notes: DDOT/Mayor press release, May 20, 2022 ('Mayor Bowser and DDOT Celebrate 100 Miles of DC Bike Lanes'), retrospective '2015 baseline' figure. Cumulative TOTAL on-street bike lane mileage (all facility types -- painted, buffered, contraflow, advisory, climbing lane, cycle track, protected -- excluding off-street trails and shared/sharrow lanes), matching the definition already used for this jurisdiction's existing 2026 real value. FLAG: this figure (63mi for 2015) is inconsistent with DDOT's own earlier Dec 2014 press release, which cited 69mi for calendar 2014 -- a decrease is implausible, most likely reflecting an unexplained recount/methodology change between the two DDOT releases rather than an actual reduction. Kept as DDOT's official retrospective baseline despite the inconsistency, since no better-sourced 2015 figure was found.
Same DDOT/Mayor press release as 2015 (May 20, 2022): 104mi total bike lanes (+62mi off-street trails tracked separately, not included in this total).

DC Council FY2024 DDOT Performance-Oversight Pre-Hearing Responses, Question 111 (Micromobility), pp.99-100 -- itemized facility-type table as of Dec 26, 2023: Advisory 2.5mi, Climbing Lane 5.6mi, Contraflow 7.3mi, existing/regular Bike Lane 62.7mi, Cycle Track 18.6mi, Protected Bike Lane 17.4mi, totaling 114.1mi (excludes 19.9mi of Shared Lane and 63mi of off-street trails, tracked separately). Best-sourced, most granular DC bike-infrastructure data point found -- an official DC Council submission with a full itemized breakdown, not a press-release round number.
